content.title: On the Geometry of Reinforcement Learning in Continuous State and Action Spaces
content.TL;DR: We prove that the state space is a low dimensional manifold and show that DDPG can effectively learn in this low dimensional space
content.abstract: Advances in reinforcement learning have led to its successful application in complex tasks  with continuous state and action spaces. Despite these advances in practice, most theoretical work pertains to finite state and action spaces. We propose  building  a theoretical understanding of continuous state and action spaces by employing a geometric lens. Central to our work is the idea that the transition dynamics induce a low dimensional manifold of reachable states  embedded in the high-dimensional nominal state space. We prove that, under certain conditions, the dimensionality of this manifold is at most the dimensionality of the action space plus one. This is the first result of its kind, linking the geometry of the state space to the dimensionality of the action space. We empirically corroborate this upper bound for four MuJoCo environments.We further demonstrate the applicability of our result by learning a policy in this low dimensional representation.   To do so we introduce an algorithm that learns a mapping to a low dimensional representation, as a narrow hidden layer of a deep neural network, in tandem with the policy using DDPG. Our experiments show that a policy learnt this way perform on par or better for four MuJoCo control suite tasks.
